story.head: The schedule did the Lightning no favors
paras: The Lightning won the teams’ first meeting this season, 6-4 in Tampa Bay on Oct 29. Both teams have won two in a row. The Lightning played last night, and the Jets are rested. Going in, the Bolts are third in the Atlantic (tied for seventh in the NHL) and the Jets seventh in the Central (tied for 24th).

The Lightning keep shots away better than almost anyone (3rd), get into a lot of chippy games (4th) and have had some of the best goaltending in the league (5th). The Jets create more chances on the penalty kill than almost anyone (2nd) and rarely ice the puck (4th), but don't block many shots (29th).

Nikita Kucherov (4 G / 16 A / 20 P in 15 GP) leads the Lightning in scoring, with seven points in his last five games. Brandon Hagel (8 G / 9 A / 17 P in 15 GP) has a team-high eight goals. For the Jets, Kyle Connor (13 G / 6 A / 19 P in 17 GP) leads the way in scoring, with seven points in his last five games. Mark Scheifele (3 G / 13 A / 16 P in 17 GP) is next in line, with eight points in his last five games.

Dennis Hildeby (2-0-1 / .885 SV% in 3 GS) will likely start for Tampa Bay, and Stuart Skinner (5-4-3 / .885 SV% in 12 GS) for Winnipeg. Skinner has a .840 save percentage in six starts against the Lightning, well under his usual .899. Don’t read much into it: a goalie’s record against one team rarely holds up.
At home, Scott Arniel likes to send Iafallo, Lowry and Björck out against the other team’s top line, so watch for them against Guentzel, Point and Kucherov.
